title: Murder Clinic
paragraphs: A mystery anthology adapting crime and detective fiction for radio, with each broadcast presenting a separate case rather than a continuing detective storyline.
Mutual sustaining mystery anthology using a different established fictional detective each week.
The run breaks into several distinct periods: Mutual sustaining run (July 21, 1942 to September 5, 1943) on [[org|org.09b709d4bde5c263|Mutual Broadcasting System]].

Names that turn up again and again in the surviving run include Frank Knight (announcer), Alvin Flanagan (director), John A. Bassett (radio adaptor), Lee Wright (radio adaptor), Ralph Barnhart (composer), Robert Stanley (conductor), and Agatha Christie (author).
Across its run, the surviving broadcasts are tied to [[org|org.09b709d4bde5c263|Mutual Broadcasting System]].

The stories often return to classic detective fiction, literary detective-story radio adaptation, rotating famous detectives, female private detective and Rosika Storey, impossible crime and alibi mystery, and Hercule Poirot investigation.
The show also sits in a wider radio history that includes Murder Clinic Mutual sustaining anthology and Wartime American network mystery radio.

If you are following the same actors and creative circles, related programs worth opening next include [[show|the-mysterious-traveler|The Mysterious Traveler]], [[show|the-shadow|The Shadow]], [[show|theater-five|Theater Five]], [[show|words-at-war|Words at War]], and [[show|yours-truly-johnny-dollar|Yours Truly, Johnny Dollar]].
